lockFileMaintenance.description: The package managers pick a refresh's versions, so the 14-day window is enforced there (each bunfig.toml, and exclude-newer in pyproject.toml). Renovate's own check cannot judge a refresh, which has no single release date, and would hold its status pending forever.
schedule: before 6am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Layer 1 — one PR per manifest area for the non-major long tail. Later rules override these for packages that span more than one area.
docs/ is a standalone package gated by its own workflow (docs-ci.yml), so its updates land on their own.

Layer 2 — packages installed in more than one manifest. Nothing here is a workspace, so a split bump leaves two manifests disagreeing at runtime with no check to catch it. No cooldown: it is our own package, published through OIDC trusted publishing, and bunfig excludes it for the same reason — a dependency should reach this repo on the same terms whether a bot or a person adds it.
The AI SDK core and its providers release in lockstep against a shared LanguageModelV4 surface. A major here can move that spec version, which is a code migration — not a lockfile bump.
The runtime and the web bridge both speak this protocol; they cannot be on different versions of it.
Build toolchain shared by web/ and every platform app UI.
`latest` tracks whatever bun is installed and is not a version to pin.

bun is pinned as a binary (Dockerfile ARG, workflow setup-bun), as an image (web/Dockerfile), and as every package.json's packageManager, which is the bun Renovate itself runs to regenerate lock files. test/unit/build-pins.test.ts requires them equal, so they move in one PR.
The runtime image installs Node from NodeSource's 24.x repo (setup_24.x); a Node major needs that URL changed too.

customManagers.description: Version pins Renovate's own managers can't see: the bun and Node versions the runtime Dockerfile installs (ARG) and the bun every workflow sets up. Each carries a `# renovate:` comment naming its source.
